newsitem.title: CHINA: Jardine Int Motor knows no reason for share fall.
newsitem.headline: Jardine Int Motor knows no reason for share fall.

text.p: Jardine International Motor Holdings Ltd said on Monday there had been no specific events to warrant Friday's sharp fall in its stock.

The stock fell HK$0.75 to HK$7.90 last Friday before rebounding to HK$8.40 on Monday. The stock hit a 1997 high of HK$10.60 on June 10 and 11 before beginning a decline of more than 20 percent to Monday's closing level.
"The stock market must tell us why it choses to do these things. There has not been any specific event or announcement in the last few days," chairman Anthony Nightingale told Reuters.
"There is no imminent announcement as far as I can recall."

Jardine International Motor said late last month it would do well this year to match its 1996 results, with profit margins under pressure in Hong Kong and conditions tough in its major European market, France.

Jardine International Motor's wholly-owned unit Zung Fu distributes Mercedes-Benz passenger and commercial vehicles in Hong Kong and its Southern Star joint venture with Mercedes-Benz in South China sells Mercedes cars in the eight provinces of South China.

"My own view is that there is no likelihood of a change in the franchise arrangement in South China," Nightingale said. "I don't see any likelihood of a change to the Zung Fu and Southern Star distributorship."
